route: RE-friction loop (docs/re-pipeline.md), round 2, track perf -- ATTEMPT 6 (captain-briefed: run the code A/B first, do not fix)
gating_rationale: Changes which function starts a PE's discovery emits, so it can change emitted C; default-ON with a per-run off switch that restores the previous discovery set exactly, mirroring its ELF twin fdeinterior (DIV-61).
hypothesis_filed: wave 39 captain: #406 (simdlane + retsplitglobal) regressed this witness by ~680 ms on top of a 341 ms drift; the shape to look at first is cumulative default-ON schedule cost.
hypothesis_verdict: confirmed-then-superseded: the wave-3 attribution of the +596 ms step to #541 (the PE base-relocation entry oracle) is CONFIRMED by an in-tree ablation A/B, but the prescribed follow-up -- "amortize the base-reloc oracle's added starts" -- does not exist. The oracle itself costs +50 ms (read symbols 0.95 -> 1.00 s). Its cost is a CASCADE: the 19 starts it recovers shift aif's gap map, aif then mints three starts INSIDE the witness's own 43,152-byte .pdata body, and funcboundflow truncates main there.
root_cause: A kuna FunctionSymbol has no extent, so nothing rejects a discovered entry that is interior to a known function. fdeinterior (DIV-61) answers this from .eh_frame on ELF; PE had no counterpart, though .pdata records [BeginAddress, EndAddress) per function. nikos_crack_me.exe declares one body at [0x140023350, 0x14002dbe0) and aif starts sub_140023e34 / sub_14002b324 / sub_14002b6a8 inside it.
fix: New P1 analysis pass pdatainterior: report the RUNTIME_FUNCTION bodies that describe exactly one function on the same AnalysisOutput::fde_bodies channel fdeinterior uses, so the existing commit-boundary filter covers PE. Eligibility mirrors the FDE test: no other named start inside, no other record BeginAddress inside, no overlap with the range kept before it. x86/x64 PE only.
profiling_method: Stage split by feeding decomp_dbg prefixes of the script kuna decompile generates (load file+options 0.15 s / read symbols 0.80 s / load function 2.91 s / decompile 6.63 s), plus a per-iteration instrument on the fullloop repeat group printing elapsed ms, the change count and the actions that reported changes.

decisions: The brief's flat branch was taken literally: the A/B came back flat, so no fix was attempted and the bar was NOT relaxed. Re-cutting `< 10000` would redefine `closed` as 'a builder tried'; five captains have declined to move it and the sixth attempt did not need it moved.

The profiler ships without an option row. `docs/agents.md` gates anything that CAN change emitted C; this times `apply` and writes a file, and its off-path is one cached read. It follows the existing env-gated debug-hook convention (`KUNA_DEFAULT_ON`, `KUNA_SYMBOLNAMEBOUND`) rather than the settable-option convention.

Rows are keyed by root variant, not by the root Action's own name: `clone_filtered` keeps the universal tree's name, so every row came back as `universal/...` until the label was taken from `ActionDatabase::set_current` instead.

The stale `/tmp/<worker>.rust.rc` from a previous attempt on this same worker id read 0 minutes into this session's suite. Any rc-file wait on a reused worker id must delete the file first or check its mtime.

`make rust-test` is RED in a repipe worktree for a reason that is not the tree: the harness exports KUNA_DECOMP_TEST, and `cpp_oracle_bin()` in the verify_w10_* tests uses it as the C++ oracle. With the C++ tree gone that fallback path does not exist, so those oracle assertions are normally skipped; pointed at kuna's own decomp_test_dbg they assert upstream spellings kuna deliberately changed (`xunknown4` vs DIV-6 `unsigned int`) and fail. Confirmed by bisection: the same test fails on unmodified HEAD and passes under `env -u KUNA_DECOMP_TEST`. Run the suite with that env var unset.
